title: Circuit Diagrams Are a Museum
thesis: The battery symbol is Volta's pile of discs seen from the side. The inductor is a coil, the resistor a folded wire — and almost none of those objects still exist.

author.note: Written directly rather than by a subagent, following the drawn-explainer skill as published.

sourcing.battery: The symbol originated as a schematic of the voltaic pile: alternating long and short lines for Volta's alternating copper and zinc discs, one pair per cell. Standard account, Wikipedia 'Voltaic pile' and Smithsonian NMAH 703289.
sourcing.resistor: The zigzag is the back-and-forth path of resistance wire wound on a core. Universally given in trade and teaching sources; no scholarly citation found, so the film leans its weight on the battery and treats this as supporting.
sourcing.inductor: A coil drawn as a coil — no derivation to dispute.
sourcing.capacitor: Two parallel plates across a gap, unchanged. Used as the episode's one deliberate non-morph.
sourcing.refused: No claim that the ground symbol depicts layers of earth, and no dating of the capacitor to the Leyden jar — a Leyden jar is not a parallel-plate capacitor.

pipeline.narration: SyncVoice (Gemini native audio, voice Kore) via D:/Projects/Utilities/textToSpeechUsingRateLimitlessTTS
pipeline.music: Lyria RealTime (models/lyria-realtime-exp), 172s bed, sidechain-ducked under the voice
pipeline.render: resvg + 24 worker threads -> libx264, 5043 frames in 46s

musicPrompt: Sparse muted electric piano, felt-damped, unhurried, wide space between notes. Soft upright bass far back, faint warm tape hiss like an old workshop radio. Curious and patient, quietly mechanical, never nostalgic or sentimental. Instrumental only, no vocals, no strong melodic hook that competes with a speaking voice.

qa.method: Whisper transcript of the final mux diffed against the script
qa.result: clean; 371 script words, 369 heard, the only difference being 'seventeen ninety nine' transcribed as '1799'
defectsFound: s04: 'zinc' spoken as 'sink' — sentence-final and unstressed
s13: 'drawings' spoken as 'brawings' — the plosive of the preceding 'The' bled into it
qa.fix: Both were ambiguous between defect and mishearing: the cross-shot test pointed at bad audio, sentence-final position pointed at artifact. Settled with the single-occurrence test — a pronunciation note into `direction`, re-synthesise, re-align just that shot. Both transcripts changed, confirming both defects and both fixes. Two TTS calls, two shot re-alignments.

notes.budget: 398 words estimated 176s with a 164-186s band, which busts the 180s cap. Trimmed to 369 before spending any TTS call; actual came in at 168.1s.
notes.nonMorph: The capacitor is the episode's one deliberate non-morph, per the gate: two plates across a gap, drawn twice two centuries apart, identical. The shot's argument is that nothing happened.
notes.craft7: Every stage keeps its object on the page at 0.34 opacity with a dashed tie to the mark it became, and each morph travels from HOME to AWAY rather than transforming in place.

youtube.title: Every circuit diagram is a drawing of something that no longer exists.
youtube.description:
The battery on a circuit diagram is Volta's 1799 pile seen from the side — long line for copper, short line for zinc, one pair per cell. The inductor is a coil of wire. The resistor is a wire folded back on itself, one peak per fold.

Almost none of those objects still exist. The battery in your pocket is not a tower of discs, and a modern resistor has no wire in it anywhere. We are still drawing the apparatus.

Not Arbitrary: things that look like meaningless convention, shown to be pictures.
